page.overview:
Who is Arkhan the Black?

Arkhan the Black, known now and forever as the "Liche King", is a Liche Lord and a powerful necromancer who was the first and most loyal of the Great Necromancer Nagash's originally mortal followers long ago in the Nehekharan capital city-state of Khemri.

When Arkhan rose from his own tomb at Nagash's command as a Liche after the Great Necromancer established himself at Nagashizzar, his first goal was to defeat the enemies of his master in Nehekhara. After Nagash's death at the hands of Alcadizaar the Conqueror, for many long years Arkhan harried Araby and the Southlands in the Wars of Death from his own citadel at the Black Tower of Arkhan, hoping to establish his own power base to retake control of the Great Land from the resurrected Tomb Kings led by Settra the Imperishable.

Arkhan was born in the great Nehekharan city-state of Khemri during the reign of King Khetep. In his youth, he was known as a rake who spent most of his time among the sacred prostitutes in the temple of Asaph, the Nehekharan goddess of beauty, magic and vengeance, mainly because his status as a member of the city's minor nobility left him no real opportunities for the pursuit of political power. It was later said that Arkhan had been forced to pay double before any of the priestesses of Asaph would touch him. Arkhan was originally nicknamed "the Black" by his peers because he used to chew the jusesh or juseh root, which stained the teeth black when consumed regularly.

When Prince Nagash, the firstborn son of King Khetep who had become the grand hierophant of Khemri's Mortuary Cult, sought a cabal of followers to assist him in usurping the throne of Khemri from his younger brother King Thutep, who had succeeded Khetep according to Nehekharan tradition, he found them in Arkhan and his fellow ne'er-do-well compatriots among the city-state's bored and hedonistic lesser nobility. In particular they were convinced to follow Nagash not only by his promises of real power and wealth, but by his demonstration of the potency of a new form of Dark Magic he had pioneered known as necromancy. Arkhan and his fellows supported Nagash by kidnapping commoners off the streets of Khemri, which served to both supply Nagash with bodies for his necromantic experiments in prolonging life and to undermine the stability of his brother's rule, greatly increasing Thutep's unpopularity due to his inability to stop the disappearances. Arkhan and the others started to learn the rudiments of necromancy themselves during this time, and he was the first of Nagash's followers after the Great Necromancer himself to partake of Nagash's greatest accomplishment, the Elixir of Life, which granted its imbibers eternal life, becoming the first of Nagash's so-called "Immortals".
